title: Pig — the dice push
parent_game: Pig, a folk dice game

credits.by: Folk game; first described in print by John Scarne, 1945

players: 2–4 players (or one big group taking turns)
equipment: 1 die (or write 1–6 on six pieces of paper, fold them, draw from a cup)
intro: Pig is one of the simplest gambling games ever made. You'll feel the texture of risk-and-reward in five minutes. Every roll is a small choice: keep what you have, or push for more.

steps.title: Set up
steps.body: Sit round a table with one die in the middle. Everyone's score starts at 0. Take turns going clockwise; the youngest goes first.
steps.svg:
<svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'>
<g transform='translate(50,60)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/>
<line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/>
<line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/>
<line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/>
<line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g>
<g transform='translate(150,60)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/>
<line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/>
<line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/>
<line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/>
<line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g>
<rect x='90' y='45' width='20' height='20' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='2'/>
<circle cx='100' cy='55' r='2' fill='#2D3127'/></svg>

steps.title: Roll
steps.body: On your turn, roll the die. Whatever you roll (2–6) is added to a temporary 'turn score' — not yet your real score.
steps.svg:
<svg viewBox='0 0 60 60' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'>
<rect x='10' y='10' width='40' height='40' rx='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='2'/>
<circle cx='20' cy='20' r='3' fill='#2D3127'/><circle cx='40' cy='20' r='3' fill='#2D3127'/>
<circle cx='30' cy='30' r='3' fill='#2D3127'/><circle cx='20' cy='40' r='3' fill='#2D3127'/>
<circle cx='40' cy='40' r='3' fill='#2D3127'/></svg>

steps.title: Bank or push?
steps.body: After each roll: BANK (add turn score to real score, end turn) or PUSH (roll again, risking everything).
steps.svg:
<svg viewBox='0 0 100 80' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'>
<rect x='15' y='25' width='70' height='40' fill='#FFF1EA' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='2' rx='3'/>
<text x='50' y='52' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='18' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>+12</text>
<text x='50' y='75' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='9' fill='#6B6960' letter-spacing='0.1em'>BANKED</text></svg>

steps.title: Push
steps.body: If you push, you roll again. As long as you don't roll a 1, you can keep pushing.
steps.svg:
<svg viewBox='0 0 100 80' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'>
<rect x='15' y='25' width='70' height='40' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='2' rx='3' stroke-dasharray='4,3'/>
<text x='50' y='52' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='18' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>+?</text>
<text x='50' y='75' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='9' fill='#6B6960' letter-spacing='0.1em'>ROLL AGAIN</text></svg>

steps.title: Bust
steps.body: If you ever roll a 1, you BUST. Your turn score evaporates. Your turn ends.
steps.svg:
<svg viewBox='0 0 60 60' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'>
<rect x='10' y='10' width='40' height='40' rx='5' fill='#FFE5DC' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='2'/>
<circle cx='30' cy='30' r='4' fill='#C75B39'/>
<text x='30' y='58' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='8' fill='#C75B39'>BUST</text></svg>

steps.title: Goal
steps.body: The first player to bank 20 points wins. Play three games.
steps.svg:
<svg viewBox='0 0 100 80' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'>
<rect x='25' y='15' width='50' height='50' fill='#FFE5DC' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='2.5' rx='4'/>
<text x='50' y='42' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='20' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>30</text>
<text x='50' y='58' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='7' fill='#7A4A1F' letter-spacing='0.1em'>FIRST TO</text>
<g transform='translate(50,73)'>
<path d='M -8 -3 L 0 4 L 8 -3' fill='none' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='2' stroke-linecap='round'/>
</g></svg>

what_to_notice: When did you feel tense?
Did pushing feel exciting or frustrating?
What made you bank?

animation.narration: Two players. First to bank 20 points wins.
Player 1 rolls a 4. Turn score = 4.
Pushes. Rolls 5. Turn score = 9.
Pushes again. Rolls 1. BUST — loses all 9.
Player 2 rolls a 5. Pushes. Rolls 3. Turn = 8.
Player 2 banks. Plays it safe. Total = 8.
Player 1 rolls 6, then 4. Banks 10. Total = 10.
Player 2 pushes hard — banks 12. Total = 20. Wins.

questions.question: What happens when a player rolls a 1 in this game?
options: They lose all the points they had built up this turn.
questions.feedback_correct: Right. The 1 is the BUST — everything in your turn-score is lost.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again — when a 1 is rolled, the player loses all the points they built up that turn.

questions.question: Why did Player 2 bank early when their turn-score was just 8?
options: They had no choice: the rules forced it.
They were far ahead, so they could play safe.
They had just watched Player 1 lose 9 points by pushing, so 8 sure points felt safer.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Banking chooses a sure 8 over the chance of more.
questions.feedback_wrong: Player 2 had just watched Player 1 push and lose all 9 points. Banking keeps 8 for certain.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Push-your-luck is the family. Every roll is a 'one more?' decision.
questions.feedback_wrong: The defining feature is the choice to keep going for more reward, with the risk of losing everything.

questions.question: If you wanted players to feel TENSE, which change would you try?
options: Make the bust cost bigger (lose all points ever banked).
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A bigger loss on a bust raises the stakes; removing the bank removes the choice. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Three-card Hanabi — hidden hands and clues
parent_game: Hanabi (a famous cooperative card game)

credits.version: A homemade cut-down: three colours, three players

equipment: 12 small paper cards — write numbers 1–4 in three colours (red, blue, green). 4 cards per colour.
a paper to track which cards have been played
intro: In Hanabi you can see everyone's cards except your own. You hold your cards facing outward: your teammates see them, and you work out yours from their clues.

steps.title: Make the cards
steps.body: On 12 small paper cards, write red 1–4, blue 1–4, green 1–4.
steps.svg:

<g><rect x='115' y='30' width='20' height='28' rx='2' fill='#3A6E8F' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1'/><text x='125' y='49' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='12' font-weight='600' fill='white'>1</text></g>
<g><rect x='140' y='30' width='20' height='28' rx='2' fill='#3A6E8F' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1'/><text x='150' y='49' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='12' font-weight='600' fill='white'>2</text></g>
<g><rect x='165' y='30' width='20' height='28' rx='2' fill='#7A8B3F' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1'/><text x='175' y='49' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='12' font-weight='600' fill='white'>1</text></g>

steps.title: Deal sideways
steps.body: Shuffle. Deal 2 cards to each of the 3 players and put the rest face down as a draw pile. Hold your cards FACING OUTWARD: your teammates see them, you don't. Put 4 clue tokens (coins or paper bits) in the middle. The player who dealt goes first; play goes clockwise.
steps.svg:
<svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'>
<g transform='translate(100,75)'><circle cx='0' cy='-25' r='10' fill='#2D3127'/>
<line x1='0' y1='-15' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/>
<line x1='-15' y1='-5' x2='15' y2='-5' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g>
<g transform='translate(60,30) rotate(-15)'><rect x='-12' y='-18' width='24' height='32' rx='2' fill='#C75B39' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='2'/>

<g transform='translate(140,30) rotate(15)'><rect x='-12' y='-18' width='24' height='32' rx='2' fill='#C75B39' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='2'/>
<text x='0' y='4' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='14' fill='white'>?</text></g>
<text x='100' y='115' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='9' fill='#6B6960' letter-spacing='0.08em'>YOU CAN'T SEE YOUR OWN CARDS</text></svg>

steps.title: Three actions
steps.body: On your turn do ONE of three things. (a) GIVE A CLUE: spend a clue token and tell one teammate about one colour or one number in their hand, pointing to every card of it ('these two are red', 'this one is a 3'). No clue when the tokens are gone. (b) PLAY a card. (c) DISCARD a card face up and take a clue token back.
steps.svg:
<svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'>
<g transform='translate(40,60)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/>

<line x1='-10' y1='0' x2='10' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g>

<rect x='70' y='35' width='60' height='30' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='2' rx='15'/>

steps.title: Play in order
steps.body: Cards are played in order, one row per colour: red 1, then red 2, red 3, red 4, and the same for blue and green. When you play a card, put it face up: if it is the next number in its colour it joins that row; if not, it is discarded and the team loses a life. You have three lives. After playing or discarding, draw a card if any are left.

steps.title: The end
steps.body: The game ends when the third life is lost, or when the draw pile is empty and everyone has had one more turn. Count the cards in the rows: that is the team's score. You can't say 'play your red 2'; that limit is the game.

what_to_notice: When did clue-giving feel hard?
When did your team click?
Did the restriction feel like a problem or like the point?

animation.narration: Three players. Cards face outward — you see others' cards, not your own.
P1 says: 'You have one red.' That's a clue to P2 about colour only.
P2 thinks: 'one of my cards is red — but which?'
P2 plays the second card — guesses it's red 1. Right!
P3 plays a card — guesses red. But it was blue 2. Lose a life.
P1 gives clue: 'two reds in your hand' — but only to P3.
The cards run out. The team has played four cards in order and kept two lives.

questions.question: Why do players hold their cards facing outward?
options: So their teammates can see what they hold but they can't see their own.
So the dealer can keep score.
Because the cards are too big to hold normally.
Because Hanabi is a betting game.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. The asymmetry of information — others see you, you don't see yourself — is the heart of the game.
questions.feedback_wrong: It's about asymmetry — teammates see your cards but you don't see them. Information is the puzzle.

questions.question: What's a clue you ARE allowed to give in this game?
options: 'Play the second card from your left.'
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Clues name only one feature — colour or number — never strategy or specific instructions.
questions.feedback_wrong: Clues name ONE feature only — a colour or a number. They never tell someone what to do.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. The team plays together, and the constraint on talking is what makes it a game.
questions.feedback_wrong: Players cooperate, but the rules limit what they can say. The constraint IS the puzzle.

questions.question: If you wanted players to feel CLEVER, which change would you try?
options: Limit clues to one feature only — they have to read between the lines.
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Clues limited to one feature leave players to work out the rest; open talk removes that. Talk about which you would try.

title: The blocking grid — workers fight for spots
parent_game: Simplified worker placement (like in Stone Age)

credits.by: Made for this tool, as a short exercise in worker placement, the mechanism of games such as Stone Age

equipment: four small objects per player, different for each player (coins, eraser bits, paper clips)
intro: Worker placement is the engine of many modern board games. The core feel: take a useful spot, and your opponent can't have it.

what_to_notice: Did blocking feel mean or fun?
When did you predict opponent's move?
Was the choice — high spot or save tokens — interesting?

animation.narration: Two players. 3×3 grid of spots. Each spot scores 3, 2, or 1 points.
P1 takes the top-left 3-point WOOD spot.
P2 takes the top-centre 3-point STONE spot.
P1 takes the top-right 3-point GOLD. All top spots gone.
P2 plays middle WOOD — settles for 2 since 3-row is full.
P1 takes middle STONE — 2 more points.
P2 takes middle GOLD. P1 plays bottom WOOD, P2 bottom STONE. Final: P1 9, P2 8.

questions.question: What happens when a player places a token on a spot?
options: The other player gets to place there too.
The spot is blocked — no one else can use it this round.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Blocking is the core. Once a spot is taken, the other player has to choose elsewhere.
questions.feedback_wrong: The whole point is that taking a spot blocks it — the other player has to pick something else.

questions.question: Why did P2 play the middle WOOD spot for 2 points instead of going for the 3-point row?
options: All the 3-point spots were blocked already.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Blocking shapes choice. P2 had to pick from what wasn't taken.
questions.feedback_wrong: All three top-row 3-point spots were already blocked. P2 had to pick from the remaining options.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Worker placement: each spot taken is a spot blocked.
questions.feedback_wrong: This is the classic worker-placement pattern — taking a spot denies it to others.

questions.question: If you wanted to make this game LESS confrontational, which change would you try?
options: Allow multiple players on one spot (no blocking).
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Letting players share a spot removes the blocking, and with it most of the contest for spots. Talk about what the game would become.

animation.narration: 5×5 grid. X starts.
X plays centre.
O plays diagonally.
X extends — two in a row diagonally.
O blocks the diagonal.
X builds in another direction — sets a trap.
A few moves later, O misses the threat down the middle. X completes four in a row. X wins.

questions.question: Why is 5×5 four-in-a-row more interesting than regular 3×3 tic-tac-toe?
options: With more space, you can plan multiple threats — strategy opens up.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. With more space, each player can build more than one threat at a time.
questions.feedback_wrong: More space lets a player build two threats at once, and the other player can block only one.

questions.question: What's the most important skill in this game?
options: Reading your opponent's plan and blocking it before it completes.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. The whole game is about seeing threats and choosing whether to block or build.
questions.feedback_wrong: It's about reading. You watch what your opponent is building and decide: block, or build your own threat?

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
options: Pattern building (you're trying to make a specific shape)
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. The game is about building a specific pattern (4-in-a-row) before your opponent.
questions.feedback_wrong: You're racing to create a specific arrangement of marks. That's pattern-building.

questions.question: If you wanted players to feel THOUGHTFUL, which change would you try?
options: Make the grid larger so multi-step plans become possible.
Use random tokens instead of choosing.
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A larger grid leaves room for longer plans; a timer cuts them short. Talk about which you would try.

what_to_notice: Did you remember earlier flips?
Did watching others teach you?
When did luck stop mattering?

animation.narration: 16 cards face-down in a 4×4. 8 pairs to find.
P1 flips top-left and top-right. ★ and ●. No match.
P2 flips middle-left and middle-centre. ▲ and ★. No match.
P1 remembers: top-left was ★. Flips top-left and middle-centre. Match!
P1 goes again. Flips two new ones. Mismatch. Turn ends.
P2 saw both — flips them. Match. P2 catches up.
Game continues — those who remember best take the most pairs.

questions.question: Why does memory matter in this game?
options: Cards stay face-down except briefly during flips. Remembering what you saw earlier helps you find pairs.
The rules require a memory test before playing.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Cards revealed once go back face-down — but the information is still in your head, if you remember.
questions.feedback_wrong: Cards flip face-up briefly, then go back. The information you saw is still useful — if you remembered it.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
options: Set collection — you collect matching pairs.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. You collect matching pairs — that's set-collection.
questions.feedback_wrong: You're collecting matching pairs. That's set-collection — gathering completed sets to score.

questions.question: After a few turns, what happens to the role of luck?
options: As more cards have been seen, skill (memory) starts to matter more than luck.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Early flips are blind. As more cards are revealed, the decisions become memory-driven.
questions.feedback_wrong: Early flips are blind. As more cards are seen, memory takes over from luck.

questions.question: If you wanted to make this game require more SKILL and less LUCK, what would you change?
options: Show cards for longer when flipped.
Hide them faster — give players less time to memorise.
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. More pairs give memory more to hold; showing cards for longer makes remembering easier. Talk about what each would change.

title: Werewolf-5 — find the traitor
parent_game: Werewolf / Mafia / Among Us

credits.by: Dmitry Davidoff, 1986, as Mafia; also played as Werewolf

equipment: 5 small paper slips — write 'wolf' on one, 'village' on four
intro: Werewolf is the social-deduction template — most players are loyal, one is hidden among them, and the table has to figure out who.

steps.title: Pass out roles
steps.body: Make 5 slips. One says 'wolf', four say 'village'. Players draw secretly. Read in private.

what_to_notice: When did you doubt yourself?
Was lying easy or hard?
Who became leaders without trying?

animation.narration: Five players sit in a circle. One is the wolf. Nobody knows who.
Day. Players talk. P1 says: 'P3 hasn't said anything.' Others nod.
P3 (the wolf) defends: 'I'm just listening — like always.'
Vote. P1, P2, P5 vote P3. P3 is OUT — and revealed as the wolf!

questions.question: What makes this game different from a normal cooperative game?
options: Players are all on the same side.
One player has a secret goal opposed to the others — the others have to deduce who it is.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. The hidden adversary is the engine — most players cooperate, one works against them in secret.
questions.feedback_wrong: There's a hidden adversary. Most players are on one team, one is secretly on another. The cooperation is partial.

questions.question: If you were the wolf, how would you play?
options: Talk normally — neither too quiet nor too eager. Deflect suspicion onto others.
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Some wolves stay quiet, some talk a lot, some accuse others. Talk about what you saw P3 do, and what you would try.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Hidden identity, deduction, and the traitor pattern all live in this family.
questions.feedback_wrong: This is the social-deduction family — a hidden traitor, the rest deducing who it is.

questions.question: If you wanted players to feel TENSE, which change would you try?
options: Make the wolf's elimination final and immediate (no second chances).
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Final eliminations make each accusation weigh more; showing every role ends the game. Talk about which you would try.

title: Paper auction — bid for the prize
parent_game: Auction / bidding games (For Sale, High Society)

credits.by: Made for this tool, after the bidding in games such as For Sale and High Society

equipment: 30 small paper bits per player (their bidding tokens)
5 'prize cards' — pieces of paper marked with values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
intro: Auctions are deceptively simple games of value. Pay too much for a prize and you've won the wrong way. Pay too little and you walk away empty-handed.

steps.title: Set up
steps.body: Each player gets 30 paper bits — these are their bidding tokens. Put 5 prize cards in a bag.

what_to_notice: When did you overpay?
Did you read the others' bidding patterns?
What did the last prize feel like?

animation.narration: Three players. Each starts with 30 tokens. Five prizes in the bag.
First prize: a 5. The biggest one. Players bid secretly.
P3 wins with 18 tokens. Pays 18. Takes the 5-prize.
Next prize: a 3. P3 has fewer tokens. P1 wins with 11.
Three more rounds. P3 has only 12 tokens left, and P1 outbids them for the 4. P2 takes the 2, P3 the 1. Final prize values: P1 7, P2 2, P3 6. P1 wins.

questions.question: What's the central tension in this game?
options: Bidding too much wastes tokens; bidding too little loses the prize.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Every bid is a balance — pay enough to win, but not so much you lose value.
questions.feedback_wrong: It's about balance. Bid too high and you waste tokens; bid too low and you lose the prize.

questions.question: Why is it risky to spend a lot on the first prize?
options: If you spend big early, you have less for later — and can't win when the biggest prize comes.
First prizes are always low value.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Tokens spent are gone. Big early spending leaves you short for later rounds.
questions.feedback_wrong: Tokens are finite. Spending a lot early means you'll be outbid on later prizes.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. The whole game runs on bidding.
questions.feedback_wrong: This is the bidding family — players spend resources to win the right to take an action.

questions.question: If you wanted players to feel CLEVER, which change would you try?
options: Show all bids openly so others can see who's bidding what.
Keep bids secret and reveal simultaneously — players have to guess what others will do.
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Secret bids make players guess each other; open bids let them react. Talk about which you would try.

title: Pick-and-pass — the drafting game
parent_game: 7 Wonders / Sushi Go (drafting card games)

credits.by: Made for this tool, after the drafting in games such as 7 Wonders and Sushi Go

equipment: 24 small paper cards — write each card with a colour and a number (4 colours × 6 numbers per colour)
a flat surface to lay cards
intro: Drafting is a compact, satisfying game pattern. You see a small set of cards, pick the one that helps your plan, pass the rest. Others get what you didn't take.

steps.title: Make 24 cards
steps.body: Make 24 paper cards: 4 colours (red/blue/green/yellow), 6 cards per colour numbered 1–6.

steps.title: Deal 6 to each player
steps.body: Shuffle and deal 6 cards to each player. With three players, use only three colours (18 cards). Look at your hand without showing anyone.

steps.body: All players simultaneously pick ONE card from their hand to keep. Pass the remaining 5 to the player on your left.

<text x='100' y='112' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='9' fill='#6B6960' letter-spacing='0.08em'>PICK ONE · PASS THE REST</text></svg>

steps.title: Repeat until cards run out
steps.body: Continue picking and passing until everyone has 6 cards. The hand shrinks each pass.

what_to_notice: Did you stick to one strategy?
Did you take cards just to deny others?
When did you change plan?

animation.narration: 4 players. 24 cards. 6 each, drafted around.
P1 holds: red 3, blue 5, green 1, green 4, yellow 2, red 6. Picks RED 6.
Pass left. P1 now sees what P4 had — 5 cards.
After five picks, P1 has red 3, red 6, red 1, red 4 and red 5. Going hard on red.
P1's last pick is red 2. Six reds for 6 points, and two runs, 1-2-3 and 4-5-6, for 4 more: 10 points. P1 wins.

questions.question: What does it mean to 'draft' a card in this game?
options: Pick one card from your hand, pass the rest.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Drafting = pick one, pass the rest. The cards rotate around the table.
questions.feedback_wrong: To draft is to pick one card from your hand and pass the rest to the next player. The hand rotates.

questions.question: Why might you keep a card you don't want?
options: You can't — you must keep useful ones.
To prevent another player from getting it.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Denying a card to your opponent is part of drafting. You can take a card just to prevent them from having it.
questions.feedback_wrong: You can take a card to deny it to others. 'Hate-drafting' is a real strategy.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Drafting is the family — pick from a shared pool, pass the rest.
questions.feedback_wrong: Drafting: pick from a rotating hand, pass the rest.

questions.question: If you wanted players to feel THOUGHTFUL, which change would you try?
options: Show every player's collection so everyone sees what each is going for.
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Showing each player's collection lets others read their plans; a timer leaves less time to think. Talk about which you would try.

title: Last-card-out — race to empty your hand
parent_game: UNO (simplified)

credits.by: A cut-down of the colour-or-number matching games, the family Uno belongs to

equipment: 30 small paper cards — write each with a colour and number (4 colours × 7 cards numbered 1–7, plus 2 wilds)
a deck pile in the middle
intro: UNO works because the rule is so simple: get rid of all your cards. The whole game is reading what's in your hand and what's on top of the pile.

steps.body: 30 cards: 4 colours (red/blue/green/yellow), 7 numbered cards each (1–7), plus 2 wilds (any colour).

A wild can be played on anything; say which colour it stands for. If you can't play, draw one card; if it matches, you may play it at once. When the draw pile runs out, shuffle the discard pile, all but its top card, to make a new one.

When did you feel stuck?

animation.narration: Two players. Each holds 5 cards. Discard pile shows: red 4.
P1 plays red 2 (matches red).
P2 plays red 1.
P1 has no red or 1 — draws a card. Now holds 5.
P1 plays blue 1 (matches the 1). P2 plays blue 6.
Race continues. P2 plays last cards first — wins by emptying hand.

questions.question: What's the goal in this game?
options: Empty your hand before others do.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Race to empty.
questions.feedback_wrong: The race is to empty your hand before others empty theirs.

questions.question: Why are wild cards valuable?
options: They can be played any turn — they break out of stuck situations.
They can be saved for later games.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Wilds save you when you have nothing matching the discard pile.
questions.feedback_wrong: Wilds are insurance — when nothing else matches, they always do. Saving them for the right moment matters.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. The whole game is the cards in your hand and what to play when.
questions.feedback_wrong: Hand management: deciding what to play and what to hold from your hand.

questions.question: If you wanted players to feel STRATEGIC, which change would you try?
options: Show all hands openly so players see what others can play.
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Open hands turn luck into planning; more wilds give more ways out. Talk about what each would change.

title: Charades — silent storytelling
parent_game: Charades / Pictionary (the classic acting game)
intro: Charades is the perfect example of a game where the constraint IS the game. Take away the words and you find new ways to communicate.

animation.narration: Two teams. Three players each. One slip. One minute.
T1A draws a slip — 'The Lion King'. Acts: claws, mane, walking proudly.
T1B guesses 'Lion King!' Right!
T2A draws — 'Harry Potter'. Acts wand-waving.
T2 takes 50 seconds — gets 'Harry Potter!' just in time.
After 6 rounds: T1 scores 4, T2 scores 3. T1 wins — but everyone laughed.

questions.question: Why is the no-talking rule the central element?
options: The constraint creates the puzzle — finding ways to communicate without words is the game.
The rule is just for politeness.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. The constraint IS the game. Take it away and you have nothing left to play.
questions.feedback_wrong: The constraint creates the puzzle. Without the no-talking rule, charades is just guessing.

questions.question: Why is this a cooperative game (within each team)?
options: Players pass cards to each other.
The whole team works together — actor and guessers — to score the point.
Players take turns being the rule-keeper.
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Within a team, everyone is on the same side — the actor signals, the guessers decode.
questions.feedback_wrong: Within each team, players cooperate. The actor sends signals; the guessers receive them. Both win or lose together.

questions.question: What kind of game-design mechanic is this?
questions.feedback_correct: Yes. Within teams: cooperation. Across teams: competition. The communication restriction is what makes the game.
questions.feedback_wrong: It's cooperative within a team, with a strong communication restriction (no words). That restriction makes the game.

questions.question: If you wanted players to feel CREATIVE, which change would you try?
options: Show what to act out openly.
Tighten the constraint — fewer ways to communicate forces invention.
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A tighter limit pushes players to invent; a longer timer gives them room. Talk about which you would try.

title: Nim — take the last stone
parent_game: Nim, an old strategy game for two

credits.by: Traditional; named by Charles L. Bouton, who worked out its theory in 1901

intro: Twelve stones in three heaps and one rule about taking them. There is no luck at all. Whoever takes the last stone wins, and after a few games you start to see that the winner was often settled several moves before the end.

steps.title: Set up
steps.body: Make three heaps: 3 stones, 4 stones and 5 stones.

steps.title: Take from one heap
steps.body: On your turn, take as many stones as you like from ONE heap, at least one. You may take the whole heap.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='40' cy='90' r='6' fill='#C75B39'/><circle cx='54' cy='90' r='6' fill='#C75B39'/><circle cx='68' cy='90' r='6' fill='#C75B39'/><circle cx='100' cy='90' r='6' fill='#2D3127'/><circle cx='114' cy='90' r='6' fill='#2D3127'/><circle cx='128' cy='90' r='6' fill='#2D3127'/><circle cx='100' cy='76' r='6' fill='#2D3127'/><circle cx='160' cy='90' r='6' fill='#2D3127'/><circle cx='174' cy='90' r='6' fill='#2D3127'/></svg>

steps.title: Never two heaps
steps.body: You may not take from two heaps in the same turn.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Last stone wins
steps.body: Whoever takes the last stone wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='40' cy='90' r='6' fill='#C75B39'/></svg>

steps.title: Play again
steps.body: Play three games, taking turns to go first. Notice when you knew how the game would end.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: When did you know who would win?
Was there a position you wanted to leave your opponent?
Did going first help?

animation.narration: Three heaps: 3, 4 and 5 stones. P1 goes first.
P1 takes 2 from the bottom heap. Heaps: 3, 4, 3.
P2 takes the whole middle heap. Heaps: 3, 0, 3.
P1 takes 1 from the top heap. Heaps: 2, 0, 3.
P2 takes 1 from the bottom heap, so the two heaps are equal: 2 and 2.
P1 takes 1 from the top. P2 takes 1 from the bottom, making them equal again: 1 and 1.
P1 has to take one stone. One is left.
P2 takes the last stone and wins.

questions.question: How many heaps may you take from in one turn?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. One heap per turn, as many stones as you like from it.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again: a turn takes from one heap only.

questions.question: Who wins?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. Taking the last stone wins.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at the last move: P2 takes the last stone and wins.

questions.question: Once the heaps were 2 and 2, what did P2 do on each turn?
options: Took the same number as P1, from the other heap, so the heaps stayed equal
Always took from the top heap
questions.feedback_correct: Right. Whatever P1 took from one heap, P2 took from the other. With equal heaps, P2 could always take the last stone.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at the heaps after each of P2's moves: 2 and 2, then 1 and 1.

questions.question: If you wanted Nim to feel less like a puzzle with one answer, what would you change?
options: Roll a die to decide how many you may take
Play the version where taking the last stone loses
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A die adds luck and weakens planning; the losing version turns the ending round; more heaps make the pattern harder to see. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Raja Mantri Chor Sipahi — find the thief
parent_game: Raja Mantri Chor Sipahi, a chit game played across India

credits.rules: As recorded by Seema Periwal and Ravi Poovaiah for D'Source, IDC, IIT Bombay

intro: Four folded chits, four roles, one guess. The Raja and the Mantri show themselves, and the Mantri then has to read the faces of the last two players and say which one is the Chor. It is mostly a game of watching people.

steps.title: Make the chits
steps.body: Write Raja 1000, Mantri 500, Sipahi 300 and Chor 0 on four slips. Fold them and mix them up.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='12' y='40' width='42' height='34' rx='2' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='33' y='61' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='8' fill='#6B6960'>RAJA</text><rect x='59' y='40' width='42' height='34' rx='2' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='80' y='61' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='8' fill='#6B6960'>MANTRI</text><rect x='106' y='40' width='42' height='34' rx='2' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='127' y='61' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='8' fill='#6B6960'>SIPAHI</text><rect x='153' y='40' width='42' height='34' rx='2' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='174' y='61' text-anchor='middle' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='8' fill='#6B6960'>CHOR</text></svg>

steps.title: Draw in secret
steps.body: Each player draws one chit and reads it without showing anyone.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Who is my Mantri?
steps.body: The Raja shows their chit and calls out 'Mera Mantri kaun hai?' (Who is my minister?). The Mantri shows their chit.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Mantri kaun hai?</text></svg>

steps.title: The guess
steps.body: The Mantri looks at the two players left and says which of them is the Chor.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>You are the Chor</text></svg>

steps.title: Score
steps.body: Everyone opens their chit. If the Mantri was right, everyone keeps the points on their chit. If wrong, the Mantri's 500 go to the Chor. Write down the scores, fold the chits again and redraw. After four rounds, the highest total wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>R1  1000</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>R2  0</text><text x='58' y='74' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>R3  300</text><text x='58' y='94' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>R4  500</text></svg>

what_to_notice: What did you watch for when you guessed?
As the Chor, what did you do with your face?
Did the points change how you played?

animation.narration: Four players draw chits. Nobody knows anyone else's role.
P1 is the Raja and calls for the Mantri.
P2 shows the Mantri chit. Now P2 must find the Chor: P3 or P4.
P2 watches P3 and P4 for a while, and guesses P3.
Wrong. P3 is the Sipahi; P4 is the Chor. The Mantri's 500 go to the Chor.
Round 1 scores: P1 1000, P2 0, P3 300, P4 500. Mix the chits for round 2.

questions.question: Who has to find the Chor?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. The Mantri guesses.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again: the Mantri has to say which player is the Chor.

questions.question: What happens to the points when the Mantri guesses wrong?
options: The Mantri's 500 go to the Chor
The Raja's 1000 go to the Mantri
questions.feedback_correct: Right. A wrong guess hands the Mantri's 500 to the Chor.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at the scores after round 1.

questions.question: After round 1, how many points did P4 have?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. P4 was the Chor, scored 0 on the chit, and took the Mantri's 500.
questions.feedback_wrong: P4 was the Chor. The chit gives 0, but the wrong guess moved the Mantri's points.

questions.question: If you wanted the guess to be harder, what would you change?
options: Add players and more roles that stay hidden
Let the Chor swap chits once
Let the Mantri ask one question first
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Larger groups add roles that stay hidden, which makes the guess harder; a question or a shown Sipahi make it easier. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Name Place Animal Thing — one letter, four words
parent_game: Name Place Animal Thing, a pen-and-paper word game played in Indian schools

credits.rules: Scoring as commonly published: 10 for an answer only you wrote, 5 for a shared one

equipment: paper and a pen for each player
intro: Everyone gets the same letter and races to write a name, a place, an animal and a thing that start with it. The scoring rewards the answer nobody else thought of.

steps.title: Draw columns
steps.body: Each player draws four columns: Name, Place, Animal, Thing.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>NAME PLACE</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>ANIMAL THING</text></svg>

steps.title: Pick a letter
steps.body: One player says the alphabet silently in their head; another says 'stop'. The letter they had reached is the letter for the round.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>stop!</text></svg>

steps.title: Write
steps.body: Everyone writes one word for each column, starting with that letter. The first to fill all four calls 'stop', and all pens go down.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>Meera</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>Mumbai</text><text x='58' y='74' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>monkey</text><text x='58' y='94' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>mug</text></svg>

steps.title: Score
steps.body: Read the answers aloud. An answer nobody else wrote scores 10, an answer someone else also wrote scores 5, and a blank or wrong answer scores 0. A Name is a person's first name. If the group disagrees about whether an answer counts, the group votes.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>10  only you</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'> 5  shared</text><text x='58' y='74' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'> 0  blank</text></svg>

steps.title: Rounds
steps.body: Play four rounds with a new letter each time. The highest total wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Did you write the first word that came, or look for a rarer one?
How did calling 'stop' change the pace?
Were there arguments about what counts?

animation.narration: The letter is M. Everyone writes.
P1 fills all four first and calls stop: Meera, Mumbai, monkey, mug.
P2 wrote Meera, Mysuru, mouse, and left Thing blank.
P3 wrote Manoj, Mumbai, monkey, mirror.
Shared answers score 5, answers nobody else wrote score 10. P1: 5+5+5+10 = 25. P2: 5+10+10+0 = 25. P3: 10+5+5+10 = 30.
Round 2 starts with a new letter.

questions.question: How is the letter chosen?
options: One player says the alphabet silently and another says stop
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 2.

questions.question: What does an answer nobody else wrote score?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. 10 for an answer only you wrote.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again: shared answers score 5, answers only you wrote score 10.

questions.question: Why did P3 score most this round?
options: P3 had two answers nobody else wrote, Manoj and mirror, and no blanks
questions.feedback_correct: Right. Two answers only P3 wrote, and no blank.
questions.feedback_wrong: P1 called stop but shared three answers. Look at which answers were P3's alone.

questions.question: If you wanted players to take more risks, what would you change?
options: Give a bonus for calling stop
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Scoring shared answers at 0 pushes people towards rare words; a bonus for stop rewards speed over rarity. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Antakshari — sing from the last letter
parent_game: Antakshari, a singing game played across India
equipment: a watch or phone to time 30 seconds
intro: One team sings two lines of a song. The other team must answer with a different song that starts with the last letter of the last word sung. The game is a chain, and it stops only when a team cannot answer in time.

steps.title: Two teams
steps.body: Split into two teams. Agree the language of the songs and the time to answer, say 30 seconds.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Start the chain
steps.body: Toss a coin to see which team starts. That team sings at least two lines of a song the others could know.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>♪ …dil</text></svg>

steps.title: Answer from the last letter
steps.body: The other team has 30 seconds to start a different song that begins with the last letter of the last word sung.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>♪ L…</text></svg>

steps.title: No repeats
steps.body: A song already sung cannot be used again, and made-up songs do not count.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Miss and score
steps.body: If a team cannot answer in time, the other team scores a point and starts a new chain. After ten minutes, the team with more points wins; equal points are a draw.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>TEAM 1   0</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>TEAM 2   1</text></svg>

what_to_notice: Did your team keep songs ready for hard letters?
Which letters were hardest?
Did the time limit make it tense or fun?

animation.narration: Team 1 starts: two lines of a song ending in the word 'dil'.
The last letter is L. Team 2 has 30 seconds to start a song with L.
Team 2's song ends in the word 'pyaar'. Now Team 1 needs a song starting with R.
Team 1 cannot find a song starting with R in 30 seconds.
Team 2 scores a point and starts a new chain.

questions.question: What must the next song begin with?
options: The first letter of the last song
The last letter of the last word sung
A letter the other team chooses
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again: 'dil' ends in L, so the next song starts with L.

questions.question: What happens when a team cannot answer in time?
options: They may sing any song instead
The other team scores a point
Nobody scores and the game restarts
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at the last frame.

questions.question: After 'pyaar', which letter did Team 1 need?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. The last letter of 'pyaar' is R.
questions.feedback_wrong: Take the last letter of the last word.

questions.question: If you wanted quieter players to join in more, what would you change?
options: Each team member must answer in turn
Allow one line instead of two
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Taking turns inside a team gives everyone a go but puts some people on the spot; whispered help shares the load; more time lowers the pressure. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Chidiya Ud — does it fly?
parent_game: Chidiya Ud (fly, bird), a finger game played across India

credits.rules: As recorded by Seema Periwal and Ravi Poovaiah for D'Source, IDC, IIT Bombay

equipment: a table or the floor to rest fingers on
intro: Everyone rests a finger on the table. The caller names something and says 'ud' (fly). If it can fly, your finger goes up; if it cannot, it stays down. The caller lifts their own finger whatever they name, to catch you out.

steps.title: Fingers down
steps.body: Sit in a close circle. Everyone rests one index finger on the same spot. One player is the caller.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: The call
steps.body: The caller names anything, a bird, an animal, a thing, followed by 'ud', and lifts their own finger as they say it: 'Tota ud!' (parrot), 'Haathi ud!' (elephant).
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Tota ud!</text></svg>

steps.title: Up or still
steps.body: Lift your finger only if the thing named can really fly. If it cannot, keep still.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Out
steps.body: Lift your finger for something that cannot fly, or keep it down for something that can, and you are out.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Last one in
steps.body: The caller goes on, faster and faster, until one player is left. Then someone else becomes the caller.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: What made you lift your finger by mistake?
As caller, which tricks worked?
Was it more about knowing or about speed?

animation.narration: Five in a circle, fingers down. C is the caller.
'Tota ud!' (parrot). A parrot flies, so every finger goes up.
'Haathi ud!' (elephant). C lifts a finger anyway. P2 lifts too, and is out.
'Patang ud!' (kite). A kite does fly. P4 keeps still and is out.
'Kursi ud!' (chair). P1 lifts a finger and is out. P3 is the last one in.

questions.question: When should you lift your finger?
options: Only when the thing named can fly
questions.feedback_correct: Right. The caller's finger is there to fool you.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again: the caller lifts a finger even for an elephant.

questions.question: Why was P4 out after 'Patang ud'?
options: A kite can fly, and P4 kept still
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: A kite flies, so fingers should go up.

questions.question: Who was left at the end?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. P3.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at the last frame.

questions.question: Is a kite something that flies? If players argue about a call, what rule would you add?
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A caller who decides keeps the game fast; a vote is slower but feels fairer; 'living things only' ends the argument and some of the fun. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Pen fight — flick it off the desk
parent_game: Pen fight, a desk game from Indian classrooms
intro: Two pens on a desk, one flick each turn. Knock the other pen off the edge and keep your own on. Here your hand decides more than your head.

steps.title: Pens down
steps.body: Put both pens on the desk, a hand's length apart.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='30' width='150' height='70' fill='#F2EADB' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><rect x='50' y='55' width='40' height='6' rx='3' fill='#C75B39' transform='rotate(-15 70 58)'/><rect x='105' y='70' width='40' height='6' rx='3' fill='#2D3127' transform='rotate(20 125 73)'/><line x1='160' y1='30' x2='160' y2='100' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='4,3'/></svg>

steps.title: One flick
steps.body: Toss a coin to see who flicks first. Take turns. On your turn, flick your own pen once with a finger, aiming to hit the other pen.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='30' width='150' height='70' fill='#F2EADB' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><rect x='50' y='55' width='40' height='6' rx='3' fill='#C75B39' transform='rotate(-15 70 58)'/><rect x='105' y='70' width='40' height='6' rx='3' fill='#2D3127' transform='rotate(20 125 73)'/><line x1='160' y1='30' x2='160' y2='100' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='4,3'/></svg>

steps.title: Off the edge
steps.body: A pen is out when its middle goes past the edge of the desk or it falls. A pen hanging over the edge with its middle still on the desk is still in.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='10' y='30' width='150' height='70' fill='#F2EADB' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><rect x='50' y='55' width='40' height='6' rx='3' fill='#C75B39' transform='rotate(-15 70 58)'/><rect x='105' y='70' width='40' height='6' rx='3' fill='#2D3127' transform='rotate(20 125 73)'/><line x1='160' y1='30' x2='160' y2='100' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='2' stroke-dasharray='4,3'/></svg>

steps.title: Win the round
steps.body: Whoever keeps their pen on the desk wins the round. If one flick sends both pens off, play the round again.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Best of five
steps.body: The first to win three rounds wins. Take turns to flick first.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P1  ✓ ✓ ✓</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P2  ✓ ✓</text></svg>

what_to_notice: Did you attack, or defend near the edge?
Did your flicks get better as you played?
How did it feel to lose to a lucky flick?

animation.narration: Round 1. The grid is the desk; the right-hand side is the edge. P1 flicks first.
P1 hits P2's pen, which slides towards the edge.
P2 flicks back and misses. Its pen ends up at the edge, middle still on the desk.
P1 flicks again and knocks P2's pen off. P1 wins round 1.
Rounds 2 to 4: P2 wins two, P1 wins one. It is 2–2.
Round 5: P2 flicks too hard and its own pen flies off. P1 wins, three rounds to two.

questions.question: When is a pen out?
options: When its middle goes past the edge, or it falls
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: What happens if one flick sends both pens off?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 4.

questions.question: How many rounds did P1 need to win the match?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. Best of five: first to three.
questions.feedback_wrong: The match is best of five, first to three rounds.

questions.question: If you wanted a player with less practice to have a fair chance, what would you change?
options: The stronger player flicks with their other hand
Two flicks a turn for the weaker player
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A handicap evens the hands; a bigger desk makes rounds longer; one round makes luck count for more. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Hand cricket — runs on your fingers
parent_game: Hand cricket, played across India
intro: Two players show a number from 1 to 6 on one hand at the same moment. If the numbers differ, the batter scores their number. If they match, the batter is out. You are guessing what the other person will show, and trying not to be guessed.

steps.title: Toss
steps.body: One player calls odd, the other even. Both show fingers and add them up. If the total is odd, the odd player wins the toss and chooses to bat or bowl.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><text x='100' y='62' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='26' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>odd?</text></svg>

steps.title: Show together
steps.body: On each ball, batter and bowler show a number from 1 to 6 with one hand at the same moment. Agree how to show 6; many players use the thumb alone.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><text x='100' y='62' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='26' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>4 · 2</text></svg>

steps.title: Runs or out
steps.body: If the numbers differ, the batter scores the number they showed. If they are the same, the batter is out.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><text x='100' y='62' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='26' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>3 · 3</text></svg>

steps.title: Swap
steps.body: When the batter is out, the other player bats and tries to pass the score.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Win
