steps.body: If the second batter passes the score, they win. If they are out first with fewer runs, the first batter wins. Equal scores are a tie.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P1  12</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P2  11</text></svg>

what_to_notice: Did you try to guess the other person's number?
Did you change your pattern after a few balls?
Was batting second easier or harder?

animation.narration: P1 bats first. P1 shows 4, P2 shows 2. Different, so P1 scores 4.
P1 shows 6, P2 shows 3. P1 scores 6: total 10.
P1 shows 2, P2 shows 5. Total 12.
P1 shows 3, P2 shows 3. Same number: P1 is out for 12.
P2 bats and needs 13 to win. P2 shows 5, P1 shows 1: 5 runs.
P2 shows 6, P1 shows 4: total 11.
P2 shows 4, P1 shows 4. P2 is out for 11.
P1 wins by one run.

questions.question: What happens when batter and bowler show the same number?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at the 3 and 3.

questions.question: P1 is batting, shows 6, and P2 shows 3. How many runs?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. The batter scores their own number.
questions.feedback_wrong: The batter scores the number they showed.

questions.question: How many runs did P2 need to win?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. One more than P1's 12.
questions.feedback_wrong: P2 had to pass 12.

questions.question: If you wanted batting to feel more like pushing your luck, what would you change?
options: Let the batter stop and keep their runs, but lose them all if out
Let the bowler show two numbers
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Letting the batter stop and bank adds a choice to every ball; three wickets make one bad guess cost less; fewer numbers make outs more likely. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Gulaam Chor — don't be left with the Jack
parent_game: Gulaam Chor (Jack Thief), an Indian card game related to Old Maid

credits.version: 24 cards, so that it fits in ten minutes

equipment: a standard deck: only Ace to 5 of each suit and the four Jacks (24 cards)
intro: Pairs are thrown away, one card is drawn blind each turn, and one Jack has no partner. Nobody wins. The game finds the one player left holding that Jack, the Gulaam Chor.

steps.title: Take out one Jack
steps.body: Use Ace to 5 of every suit and the four Jacks. Take out one Jack without looking at it and put it aside. Shuffle and deal all the cards.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-12.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>A</text></g><g transform='rotate(-6.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>3</text></g><g transform='rotate(0.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>5</text></g><g transform='rotate(6.0 159 100)'><rect x='142' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>J</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Throw pairs
steps.body: Everyone puts down any two cards of the same rank, whatever their suits. If you have three of a rank, put down two and keep one.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-6.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>4</text></g><g transform='rotate(0.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>4</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Draw blind
steps.body: Hold your cards fanned, face down to the others. The player to the dealer's left starts: draw one card from the next player's hand without seeing it. If it makes a pair, put the pair down. Then the next player draws, and so on round the circle.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Safe
steps.body: A player whose hand is empty is safe and sits out.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: The thief
steps.body: When every pair is down, one Jack is left. Whoever holds it is the Gulaam Chor and loses.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-3.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>J</text></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Did you try to hide where the Jack sat in your hand?
Could you tell who had it?
How did it feel to play a game you could only lose?

animation.narration: The pairs are down. Three Jacks are left: two will pair up, one cannot. P1 draws from P2.
P1 draws P2's 3, pairs it with the other 3 and puts the pair down.
P2 draws P3's 5 and puts down a pair of 5s.
P3 draws P1's Jack and pairs it with their own. P1 and P3 have empty hands and are safe.
P2 is left holding the last Jack. P2 is the Gulaam Chor.

questions.question: Why is one Jack taken out before dealing?
options: So one Jack can never be paired
questions.feedback_correct: Right. Three Jacks make one pair and one left over.
questions.feedback_wrong: Count the Jacks: with one removed, three are left.

questions.question: What happens when a drawn card makes a pair?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: Who was the Gulaam Chor?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. P2 held the last Jack.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at the last frame.

questions.question: The game has one loser and no winner. If you wanted a winner too, what would you change?
options: The first player to empty their hand wins
Score a point for each pair put down
Add a second card that cannot pair
Let players swap two cards once
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A first-out winner adds a race; scoring pairs rewards luck in the deal; a second odd card means two people lose. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Satte pe Satta — build out from the sevens
parent_game: Satte pe Satta (Badam Satti), an Indian card game related to Sevens

credits.version: Only the 4 to 10 of each suit, 28 cards

equipment: a standard deck: only 4 to 10 of each suit (28 cards)
intro: Every row starts from a seven and grows one card at a time, down to 4 and up to 10. You must play if you can, so the cards you hold back decide who gets stuck.

steps.title: Deal
steps.body: Use the 4 to 10 of each suit. Shuffle and deal all 28 cards, seven each.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-9.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>4</text></g><g transform='rotate(-3.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>7</text></g><g transform='rotate(3.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>10</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Open
steps.body: Whoever holds the 7 of hearts plays it first. That starts the hearts row.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-3.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>7♥</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Grow a row
steps.body: On your turn, play a seven to start a new suit, or the next card up or down on a row already started: 6 or 8 beside the 7, then 5 or 9, and so on.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-9.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>6</text></g><g transform='rotate(-3.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>7</text></g><g transform='rotate(3.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>8</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Must play
steps.body: If you can play, you must. Pass only when you have nothing that fits.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: First out
steps.body: The first player to play all their cards wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Did you hold back a seven to block the others?
When did you get stuck?
Is it fair that you must play when you can?

animation.narration: Seven cards each. Colours stand for suits: red hearts, blue spades, green clubs, yellow diamonds.
P1 holds the 7 of hearts and opens the hearts row.
P2 could play the 8 of hearts, and starts the spades row with a 7 instead.
P3 starts clubs with the 7 of clubs.
P4 has no 6 or 8 in hearts, spades or clubs. The 7 of diamonds is the only card that fits, so P4 must play it.
P1 plays the 8 of clubs. Play goes on until someone runs out of cards.

questions.question: Who plays first?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 2.

questions.question: Why did P4 play the 7 of diamonds?
options: It was the only card P4 could play, and you must play if you can
questions.feedback_correct: Right. Nothing else in P4's hand fitted a row.
questions.feedback_wrong: Check P4's cards against the rows: only the 7 of diamonds fits.

questions.question: The hearts row has the 7 and 8. Which hearts can be played next?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. One step down or one step up.
questions.feedback_wrong: Rows grow one card at a time, in both directions.

questions.question: If you wanted fewer turns where a player is stuck, what would you change?
options: A stuck player takes a card from a neighbour
Allow passing even when you could play
Start all four sevens at once
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Taking a card helps the stuck player but hurts the neighbour; free passing lets people block on purpose; opening all four rows gives everyone more places to play. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Dots and Boxes — close the square
parent_game: Dots and Boxes, a pencil-and-paper game first published in 1889

credits.by: Édouard Lucas, French mathematician; first published in the 19th century as la pipopipette

intro: Two players draw lines between dots. Whoever draws the fourth side of a box claims it and must draw again. For most of the game nobody wants to draw a box's third side.

steps.title: Dots
steps.body: Draw a square of 4 by 4 dots. That makes 9 boxes.

steps.title: One line
steps.body: Toss a coin to see who starts. Take turns drawing one line, across or down, between two dots next to each other. No diagonals.

steps.title: Close a box
steps.body: If your line closes the fourth side of a box, write your initial in it and draw another line.

steps.title: Keep going
steps.body: You can close several boxes in a row, drawing again after each one.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5' fill='none'><line x1='20.5' y1='33.5' x2='179.5' y2='33.5'/><line x1='20.5' y1='86.5' x2='179.5' y2='86.5'/><line x1='20.5' y1='33.5' x2='20.5' y2='86.5'/><line x1='73.5' y1='33.5' x2='73.5' y2='86.5'/><line x1='126.5' y1='33.5' x2='126.5' y2='86.5'/><line x1='179.5' y1='33.5' x2='179.5' y2='86.5'/></g><text x='47.0' y='65.0' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>X</text><text x='100.0' y='65.0' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>X</text><text x='153.0' y='65.0' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='14' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>X</text></svg>

steps.title: Most boxes
steps.body: When every line is drawn, whoever has more boxes wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P1  5</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P2  4</text></svg>

what_to_notice: When did you start avoiding the third side of a box?
Did you ever give boxes away on purpose?
Who controlled the end of the game?

animation.narration: Nine empty boxes. The lines are not drawn here; a box shows only when someone claims it.
Many lines later, every box has two sides drawn. Any line now makes a third side somewhere and gives a box away.
P2 draws a third side on the top-left box. P1 closes it, marks it, and draws again.
P1's extra line closes the next box too. P1 takes it and draws again.
Now P1 has to give something away. P2 closes the three boxes of the bottom row, one after another.
The last four go back and forth. Final count: P1 5, P2 4.

questions.question: What happens when your line closes a box?
options: You claim the box and draw again
The box goes to the other player
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: Why do players avoid drawing a box's third side?
options: The other player can then close it
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Think about who draws the fourth side next.

questions.question: What was the final score?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Count the boxes in the last frame.

questions.question: If you wanted the ending to depend less on who is forced to give boxes away, what would you change?
options: Closing a box ends your turn
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Ending the turn after a box removes the chains; a pass lets you dodge one bad move; a bigger grid makes the end harder to count. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Battleship on paper — find the hidden fleet
parent_game: Battleship, the pencil-and-paper game

credits.version: A 6 by 6 grid and three ships

intro: Each player hides three ships on a small grid and fires at the other's grid by calling squares. All you learn is 'hit' or 'miss', and from that you work out where the ships are.

steps.title: Two grids
steps.body: Each player draws two grids of 6 by 6 squares, A to F across and 1 to 6 down: one for your ships, one for your shots. The usual game uses 10 by 10; this smaller one fits in ten minutes.

steps.title: Hide ships
steps.body: Without showing anyone, mark one ship 3 squares long and two ships 2 squares long, each across or down, not overlapping.

steps.title: Call a square
steps.body: Toss a coin to see who starts. Take turns calling one square, like C4. The other player says 'hit' or 'miss'. Mark it on your shots grid with a cross for a hit and a dot for a miss.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>C4?</text></svg>

steps.title: Sunk
steps.body: When every square of a ship has been hit, its owner says 'sunk'.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>sunk</text></svg>

steps.title: Win
steps.body: The first to sink all three of the other player's ships wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: After a hit, how did you choose the next square?
Did you hide your ships in a pattern?
How much was luck at the start?

animation.narration: P1's record of shots at P2's grid. Nothing is known yet. (P2 is firing at P1 too.)
P1 calls C3. Miss.
Next turn P1 calls C2. Hit.
P1 tries the squares beside the hit: C1 misses, D2 hits.
B2: hit, and P2 says 'sunk'. The 3-long ship ran from B2 to D2.
Later P1 finds the two short ships, at E4–E5 and A6–B6, and sinks the last one before P2 finishes. P1 wins.

questions.question: What does the other player tell you after you call a square?
options: How far away the nearest ship is
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: After the hit at C2, why did P1 try the squares around it?
options: Ships lie across or down, so the rest of the ship must be next to the hit
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Think about how ships are placed.

questions.question: Which squares did the 3-long ship cover?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at the frame where P2 says 'sunk'.

questions.question: If you wanted less luck at the start, what would you change?
options: Give each player one free clue, such as a row that holds a ship
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A clue shortens the blind start; a bigger grid lengthens it; an extra shot on a hit rewards the lucky early hit even more. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Bulls and Cows — crack the code
parent_game: Bulls and Cows, the pencil-and-paper game Mastermind was based on
intro: Each player writes a secret four-digit number with no digit repeated. You guess the other player's number, and they tell you how many digits are right and in the right place (bulls) and how many are right but in the wrong place (cows). You work out the number from these counts.

steps.title: Secret number
steps.body: Each player secretly writes a four-digit number using four different digits, such as 4271. Agree whether it may start with 0.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>4 2 7 1</text></svg>

steps.title: Guess
steps.body: Toss a coin to see who starts. Take turns guessing the other player's number, also with four different digits.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>1234?</text></svg>

steps.title: Bulls and cows
steps.body: The other player answers with a count: a bull for each right digit in the right place, a cow for each right digit in the wrong place. They do not say which digits.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>1 bull, 2 cows</text></svg>

steps.title: Write it down
steps.body: Keep a list of your guesses and the answers. Use them to rule digits in and out.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>1234  1B 2C</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>5678  1B 0C</text></svg>

steps.title: Win
steps.body: The first to get four bulls wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Which guess told you the most?
Did you guess to win, or guess to learn?
Did you keep notes, or hold it in your head?

animation.narration: P2's secret number is 4271. P1 does not know it.
P1 guesses 1234. P2 answers: 1 bull, 2 cows. Three of these digits are in the number, one of them in the right place.
P1 guesses 5678. 1 bull, 0 cows. Exactly one of 5, 6, 7, 8 is in the number, in the same place as here.
P1 guesses 4217. 2 bulls, 2 cows. All four digits are right; two are in the wrong place.
P1 swaps the last two: 4271. Four bulls. P1 wins.

questions.question: What is a cow?
options: A right digit in the right place
A right digit in the wrong place
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: The number is 4271 and the guess is 1234. What is the answer?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. The 2 is in the right place; the 1 and 4 are in the number but in other places.
questions.feedback_wrong: Compare digit by digit: only the 2 sits in the same place.

questions.question: What did '5678: 1 bull, 0 cows' tell P1?
options: None of 5 to 8 is in the number
Exactly one of 5, 6, 7, 8 is in the number, in the same place as in 5678
All four are in the number
questions.feedback_correct: Right. It was the 7, third place.
questions.feedback_wrong: One bull means one digit right and in place; no cows means no others.

questions.question: If you wanted it quicker for younger players, what would you change?
options: Say which digit is the bull
Limit each player to six guesses
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Three digits shrink the puzzle; naming the bull gives away most of the reasoning; repeats make it harder, not easier. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Go Fish — ask for what you need
parent_game: Go Fish, a children's card game

credits.version: Ace to 6 of each suit, 24 cards

equipment: a standard deck: only Ace to 6 of each suit (24 cards)
intro: You collect all four cards of a rank by asking the other players for them. Every question you ask also tells everyone what you are collecting.

steps.title: Deal
steps.body: Use Ace to 6 of each suit. Deal five cards to each player and put the rest face down in a pile: the pond.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-15.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>A</text></g><g transform='rotate(-9.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>2</text></g><g transform='rotate(-3.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>4</text></g><g transform='rotate(3.0 159 100)'><rect x='142' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>4</text></g><g transform='rotate(9.0 193 100)'><rect x='176' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='193' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>6</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Ask
steps.body: The player to the dealer's left starts, then play goes left. On your turn, ask one player for a rank you already hold: 'Do you have any 4s?'
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Any 4s?</text></svg>

steps.title: Hand over or go fish
steps.body: If they have any, they must give you all of them, and you ask again. If not, they say 'Go fish' and you draw from the pond. Drawing the rank you asked for lets you go again; otherwise the turn passes left.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Go fish</text></svg>

steps.title: Books
steps.body: When you have all four of a rank, put them down: that is a book.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-12.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>4</text></g><g transform='rotate(-6.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>4</text></g><g transform='rotate(0.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>4</text></g><g transform='rotate(6.0 159 100)'><rect x='142' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>4</text></g></svg>

steps.title: End
steps.body: If your hand runs out while the pond still has cards, draw one and carry on. Play until all six books are down. Whoever has the most books wins; equal counts are a draw.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: What did other players' questions tell you?
Did you ever avoid asking, to keep your hand secret?
How much did the pond decide?

animation.narration: P1 holds two 4s, a 2, a 6 and an Ace. P1 asks P2: 'Any 4s?'
P2 has one 4 and hands it over. P1 asks again: 'P3, any 4s?'
P3 has the last 4. P1 now has all four and puts down a book.
P1 asks P2 for 6s. 'Go fish.' P1 draws a 2 from the pond, not a 6, so the turn passes to P2.
P2 heard P1 ask for 6s, so P2 knows P1 holds one. P2 asks P1 for 2s and gets two.

questions.question: What may you ask for?
options: Only a rank you already hold
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 2.

questions.question: After 'Go fish', why did P1's turn end?
options: P1 drew a 2, not the 6 asked for
questions.feedback_correct: Right. Only drawing the rank you asked for lets you go again.
questions.feedback_wrong: What did P1 draw?

questions.question: What is a book?
options: All four cards of one rank
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 4.

questions.question: Asking tells the others what you hold. If you wanted that to matter more, what would you change?
options: Let a player lie once per game
Steal a card from anyone who forgot what was asked
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Secret asking removes the information; one lie makes every question less certain; a memory rule rewards listening. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Cheat — play face down, lie if you like
parent_game: Cheat (also called Bluff), a card game

credits.version: Ace to 8 of each suit, 32 cards

equipment: a standard deck: only Ace to 8 of each suit (32 cards)
intro: Cards go down face down while you say what they are, and you may be telling the truth or not. Anyone can call 'Cheat!' and turn them over, and whoever was wrong takes the whole pile.

steps.title: Deal
steps.body: Use Ace to 8 of each suit. Deal all the cards.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-9.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>A</text></g><g transform='rotate(-3.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>5</text></g><g transform='rotate(3.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>8</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Say the rank
steps.body: The player to the dealer's left starts. They put one or more cards face down on a pile and say 'One Ace' or 'Two Aces'. The next player must play 2s, the next 3s, and so on up to 8, then back to Ace.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Two 3s</text></svg>

steps.title: Lie if you like
steps.body: The cards do not have to be what you say.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-6.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>?</text></g><g transform='rotate(0.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>?</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Call 'Cheat!'
steps.body: Before the next player plays, anyone may call 'Cheat!'. Turn the cards over. If any card is not what was said, the player who played them takes the whole pile. If they were all true, the caller takes it.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Cheat!</text></svg>

steps.title: Win
steps.body: The first to get rid of all their cards wins, as long as that last play is not caught as a lie.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: How did you decide when to call?
Did anyone lie with a straight face?
Were you more careful with a big pile?

animation.narration: P1 plays two cards face down and says 'Two 3s'. They really are 3s.
P2 must play 4s and has none. P2 plays the Ace face down and says 'One 4'. A lie.
P3 holds two of the four 4s, so a 4 from P2 seems less likely. P3 calls 'Cheat!' The card is an Ace. P2 takes the whole pile: the two 3s and the Ace.
P3 must play 5s, plays the two 4s and says 'Two 5s'. Nobody calls, so the lie stands.

questions.question: When 'Cheat!' is called and the cards were all true, who takes the pile?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. A wrong call costs the caller.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 4.

questions.question: Why did P3 doubt P2?
options: P3 held two of the four 4s, so a 4 from P2 was less likely
questions.feedback_correct: Right. What you hold tells you what others probably do not.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at P3's hand.

questions.question: After the call, who took the pile?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. P2 lied and was caught.
questions.feedback_wrong: The card was an Ace, not a 4.

questions.question: If you wanted lying to be riskier, what would you change?
options: A caught liar also misses a turn
Anyone may peek at one card before calling
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A missed turn raises the cost of being caught; one card per play makes lies smaller; a peek turns the call into a sure thing. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Snap — spot the match first
parent_game: Snap, a children's card game

credits.by: Traditional; perhaps a simpler form of the older Snip Snap Snorem

equipment: a standard deck, or half of one for a short game
intro: Everyone turns cards over onto their own pile, one at a time. When two piles show the same rank on top, the first to shout 'Snap!' wins both piles. There is no choice in which card to play; the game is in watching.

steps.title: Deal
steps.body: Deal the cards face down as evenly as you can. Nobody looks at their stack.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-9.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>?</text></g><g transform='rotate(-3.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>?</text></g><g transform='rotate(3.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>?</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Turn over
steps.body: In turn, each player turns the top card of their stack face up onto their own pile.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-3.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>9</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Snap
steps.body: When the top cards of any two piles have the same rank, the first player to shout 'Snap!' takes both piles and puts them under their stack.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Snap!</text></svg>

steps.title: Run out
steps.body: If your stack runs out, turn your pile over and keep going. A player with no cards at all is out.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Win
steps.body: Whoever ends up with all the cards wins. For a short game, stop at five minutes and count cards.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Where did you look while waiting?
Did anyone shout too early?
Was there anything to decide?

animation.narration: P1 turns over a 5. P2 turns over a 9.
P1 turns over a 2. P2 turns over a 2. Two 2s on top.
P2 shouts 'Snap!' first and takes both piles, four cards in all.
Play goes on. At five minutes P1 has 22 cards and P2 has 30. P2 wins this short game.

questions.question: When do you shout 'Snap!'?
options: When your own card is high
When the top cards of two piles have the same rank
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: What does the first to shout get?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: Do you choose which card to turn over?
options: No: you turn over the top card, and the skill is in watching
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 2.

questions.question: Snap rewards the fastest player every time. If you wanted a slower player to have a chance, what would you change?
options: A wrong shout costs a card
Each player may shout once per round
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A cost for wrong shouts slows the quick and careless; teams share the speed; more kinds of match give more chances to everyone. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Twenty Questions — yes or no
parent_game: Twenty Questions, a parlour game
intro: One player thinks of something. Everyone else may ask up to twenty questions that can be answered yes or no, and must name it before the questions run out.

steps.title: Think of something
steps.body: One player, the answerer, thinks of a person, place, animal or object and keeps it secret.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Ready</text></svg>

steps.title: Ask yes or no
steps.body: The others take turns asking questions that can be answered yes or no. The answerer must answer truthfully.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Is it alive?</text></svg>

steps.title: Count
steps.body: Keep count. A guess counts as a question.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>1 2 3 4 5</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>6 7 8 …</text></svg>

steps.title: Win
steps.body: Whoever names it within twenty questions wins and becomes the next answerer. If twenty pass, the answerer wins and goes again.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Which questions cut the possibilities in half?
Did anyone guess too early?
Was it more fun to ask or to answer?

animation.narration: A thinks of something and keeps it secret.
Question 1, P1: 'Is it alive?' A: 'No.'
Question 2, P2: 'Is it found in a kitchen?' 'Yes.'
Question 3, P3: 'Is it used for cooking?' 'Yes.' Question 4, P1: 'Does it make a sound?' 'Yes.'
Question 5, P2: 'Is it a pressure cooker?' 'Yes.' P2 named it on the fifth question and is the next answerer.

questions.question: What kind of questions may you ask?
options: Only questions answered yes or no
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 2.

questions.question: Does a guess count as a question?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: On which question was it named?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Count the questions in the animation.

questions.question: If you wanted the answerer to have a more interesting job, what would you change?
options: They score a point for every question asked
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. 'Sometimes' makes answers less certain; one lie turns every answer into a question; points for each question give the answerer something to play for. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Hangman — guess the word letter by letter
parent_game: Hangman, a pencil-and-paper word game
intro: One player picks a word and draws a dash for each letter. The others call letters. Right letters fill the dashes; wrong ones add a mark towards a limit. The guessers win if they finish the word before the limit.

steps.title: Dashes
steps.body: The chooser thinks of a word and draws one dash for each letter.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>_ _ _ _ _</text></svg>

steps.title: Call a letter
steps.body: Guessers take turns calling a letter, or guessing the whole word. A wrong guess at the whole word counts as a wrong guess.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>A?</text></svg>

steps.title: Right or wrong
steps.body: A right letter is written on every dash where it appears. A wrong letter is written to one side and adds one mark. Many people draw a hanged figure, a line per mistake; a row of tally marks works just as well.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>_ A _ _ O</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>E S  ||</text></svg>

steps.title: Limit
steps.body: Agree the limit before starting, say six wrong guesses.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>| | | | | |</text></svg>

steps.title: Win
steps.body: The guessers win if they complete the word first. The chooser wins if the limit is reached.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Which letters did you call first, and why?
When did you guess the whole word?
As chooser, how did you pick a hard word?

animation.narration: The word has five letters. The top row is the word; the bottom row keeps wrong guesses.
'A?' Yes: the second letter.
'E?' No. One wrong guess.
'O?' Yes: the last letter. 'S?' No. Two wrong.
'N?' Yes. 'T?' No. Three wrong.
A guesser reads _ A N _ O and says 'Mango'. Right, with three wrong guesses out of six.

questions.question: What happens when a called letter is in the word?
options: It is written on every dash where it appears
Only the first one is shown
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: How many wrong guesses were made?
questions.feedback_correct: Right: E, S and T.
questions.feedback_wrong: Count the letters in the bottom row.

questions.question: When does the chooser win?
options: When the wrong guesses reach the agreed limit
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 5.

questions.question: If you wanted guessers to think harder about each letter, what would you change?
options: Common letters cost two marks when wrong
Let guessers give up a turn to see one letter
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Dearer common letters stop the easy E-A-O start; a lower limit raises the stakes; a topic gives guessers more to reason with. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Spoons — grab a coin when someone makes four
parent_game: Spoons, a party card game, played here with coins

credits.version: Coins in place of spoons, a substitute Pagat lists

equipment: coins or pebbles, one fewer than the players
intro: Cards move quickly round the circle, one at a time, while everyone tries to collect four of a kind. In the middle sit coins, one fewer than the players. When one player takes a coin, everyone else grabs one too, and whoever is left without one loses the round.

steps.title: Set up
steps.body: Deal four cards to each player and put the rest face down by the dealer. Put one fewer coin than there are players in the middle.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='40' cy='90' r='6' fill='#C75B39'/><circle cx='54' cy='90' r='6' fill='#C75B39'/><circle cx='68' cy='90' r='6' fill='#C75B39'/></svg>

steps.title: Pass along
steps.body: The dealer draws a card from the pile, keeps four, and passes one card face down to the left. Each player picks up the card passed to them, keeps four, and passes one on. The last player puts their card on a waste pile; when the dealer's pile runs out, the waste pile is turned over and used again. Nobody waits for turns.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-12.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>7</text></g><g transform='rotate(-6.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>7</text></g><g transform='rotate(0.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>K</text></g><g transform='rotate(6.0 159 100)'><rect x='142' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>2</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Four of a kind
steps.body: When you hold four cards of the same rank, quietly take a coin from the middle.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-12.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>7</text></g><g transform='rotate(-6.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>7</text></g><g transform='rotate(0.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>7</text></g><g transform='rotate(6.0 159 100)'><rect x='142' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='159' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>7</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Grab
steps.body: As soon as anyone takes a coin, everyone else may grab one too.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Left out
steps.body: The player without a coin loses the round.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Were you watching the cards or the coins?
How did the speed feel?
Did anyone take a coin without four of a kind?

animation.narration: Four players, three coins in the middle. Cards start moving left.
P1 picks up a 7, keeps it, and passes the King on.
P1 picks up the last 7, passes the 2, and has four 7s. P1 quietly takes a coin.
P3 sees the coin is gone and grabs one. P2 grabs the last.
P4 was watching the cards, not the coins, and has none. P4 loses the round.

questions.question: How many coins are in the middle?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 1.

questions.question: What may you do as soon as anyone takes a coin?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 4.

questions.question: Who lost the round?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at the last frame.

questions.question: If you wanted it calmer, what would you change?
options: Pass in turns, one player at a time
Play without coins: the first to four wins
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Passing in turns removes the rush; face-up cards turn it into planning; dropping the coins removes the moment when everyone grabs. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Telephone — whisper it along
parent_game: Telephone, a party game
intro: A short message is whispered from person to person, once each. The last person says aloud what reached them, and the first says what was sent. Nobody wins; the fun is in what changed on the way.

steps.title: Sit together
steps.body: Sit in a line or a circle.
