steps.title: The message
steps.body: The first player makes up a short sentence and whispers it once to the next player.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>lunch at two…</text></svg>

steps.title: Pass it on
steps.body: Each player whispers what they heard, once, to the next. No repeating, no asking again.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Compare
steps.body: The last player says out loud what they heard. The first player says the original.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>…the zoo?</text></svg>

steps.title: Again
steps.body: Change who starts, and play again.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Where did the message change most?
Did people pass on what they heard, or what made sense to them?
Was it more fun when it changed a lot?

animation.narration: P1 whispers: 'Lunch is at two near the library.'
P2 passes on exactly what they heard.
P3 hears 'Lunch is at the zoo near the library' and passes that on.
P4 passes on 'The lunch is at the zoo, very early.'
P5 says it aloud: 'The lunch is at the zoo, very early.' P1 says the original, and everyone compares.

questions.question: How many times may you whisper the message?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: Who says the final message aloud?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 4.

questions.question: Who wins?
options: Nobody: the game is in comparing
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at the introduction.

questions.question: If you wanted the message to change less, what would you change?
options: Write it down instead of whispering
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A repeat or a shorter message keeps it whole; writing removes the mishearing that makes the game. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Fizz Buzz — count, but not by 3 or 5
parent_game: Fizz Buzz, a counting game
intro: Count round the circle, but say 'fizz' for numbers that divide by 3, 'buzz' for those that divide by 5, and 'fizzbuzz' for those that divide by both. Hesitate or slip, and you are out.

steps.title: Circle
steps.body: Stand or sit in a circle.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Count
steps.body: Count up from 1, one number each, going round.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>one, two…</text></svg>

steps.title: Replace
steps.body: Say 'fizz' instead of any number that divides by 3, 'buzz' instead of any that divides by 5, and 'fizzbuzz' instead of any that divides by both, like 15.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>fizzbuzz</text></svg>

steps.title: Out
steps.body: Say the wrong thing, or wait too long, and you are out. The next player carries on with the next number.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: End
steps.body: Play until one player is left, or stop at 50.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Was it harder to count or to remember the rule?
Did the pace speed up?
Did anyone get out on a number that was easy?

animation.narration: P1 starts: 'One.'
P2: 'Two.' P3: 'Fizz' for 3.
P4: 'Four.' P5: 'Buzz' for 5.
P1: 'Fizz' (6). P2: 'Seven.' P3: 'Eight.' P4: 'Fizz' (9).
P5 says 'Ten'. It should be 'buzz'. P5 is out.
P1 carries on: 'Eleven.' Four players left.

questions.question: What do you say for 9?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. 9 divides by 3.
questions.feedback_wrong: Does 9 divide by 3, by 5, or both?

questions.question: What do you say for 15?
questions.feedback_correct: Right. 15 divides by both 3 and 5.
questions.feedback_wrong: 15 divides by 3 and by 5.

questions.question: Why was P5 out?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: 10 divides by 5.

questions.question: If you wanted nobody to sit out for long, what would you change?
options: A slip costs a point instead of putting you out
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Points keep everyone playing; an extra rule or more speed make slips more likely, which suits a group that wants it harder. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Two Truths and a Lie — spot the false one
parent_game: Two Truths and a Lie, a get-to-know-you game
equipment: nothing, or paper to jot your three statements
intro: Each player says three things about themselves. Two are true and one is not. The others decide which is the lie.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.body: Each player thinks of three statements about themselves: two true, one false.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>1 ...</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>2 ...</text><text x='58' y='74' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>3 ...</text></svg>

steps.title: Say them
steps.body: One player says all three, in any order.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>I cannot swim</text></svg>

steps.title: Vote
steps.body: The others talk briefly, then each points to the one they think is false.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Reveal
steps.body: The speaker says which was the lie. Each right guess scores a point, if you are keeping score.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Ladakh!</text></svg>

steps.title: Next
steps.body: The next player takes a turn, until everyone has had one.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: What made a statement sound false?
Did you make your lie sound ordinary or surprising?
Did you learn anything you will remember?

animation.narration: P1: 'I have been to Ladakh.'
P1: 'I cannot swim.'
P1: 'I have two brothers.'
P2 and P3 vote for 'cannot swim'. P4 votes for 'Ladakh'.
P1 has never been to Ladakh. P4 guessed right and scores a point.

questions.question: How many of the three statements are true?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at the introduction.

questions.question: Which statement was P1's lie?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at the last frame.

questions.question: Who scored?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Who voted for Ladakh?

questions.question: If you wanted the speaker to score too, what would you change?
options: The speaker scores for each player fooled
The speaker loses a point for each right guess
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Scoring for fooling people turns it into a bluffing game; no scoring keeps it a way to meet people. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Ghost — add a letter, don't finish the word
parent_game: Ghost, a spoken word game
equipment: nothing (a dictionary if the group wants one)
intro: Players add one letter at a time to a growing string. The string must always be the start of a real word, but whoever completes a word of four or more letters loses the round.

steps.title: Agree
steps.body: Agree that words of three letters or fewer do not count, and which dictionary settles arguments.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Add a letter
steps.body: Toss a coin to see who starts. The first player says a letter. Each next player, going round, adds one letter to the end.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>P-L-A</text></svg>

steps.title: Don't finish
steps.body: The letters must always be the start of a real word. If you complete a word of four or more letters, you lose the round.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>P-L-A-N</text></svg>

steps.title: Challenge
steps.body: Instead of adding a letter, you may challenge the last player to name a word that starts with the letters so far. If they cannot, they lose the round; if they can, you lose it.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Challenge!</text></svg>

steps.title: G-H-O-S-T
steps.body: Each round you lose earns you the next letter of GHOST. Spell GHOST and you are out. The last player in wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P1  G</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P2  G H</text></svg>

what_to_notice: Did you plan ahead to a long word?
When did you bluff with a letter?
When did you challenge?

animation.narration: P2 adds L: 'PL'.
P3 adds A: 'PLA'. 'PLAN', 'PLAY' and 'PLATE' all start this way.
P4 adds N: 'PLAN'. That is a word of four letters, so P4 loses the round and takes a G.
Round 2. P1: 'Q'. P2, not sure what to add, says Z: 'QZ'.
P3 challenges. P2 cannot name a word starting with QZ, so P2 loses the round and takes a G.

questions.question: What happens if you complete a word of four or more letters?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: Why did P4 lose round 1?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at the fourth frame.

questions.question: What happens when a challenged player cannot name a word?
options: The challenged player loses the round
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 4.

questions.question: If you wanted the rounds to last longer, what would you change?
options: Only words of six letters or more count
Allow letters to be added at the front too
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A longer minimum pushes the danger later; adding letters at the front, as in the variant called Superghost, opens many more words; removing challenges takes away the bluff. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Cram — the last domino wins
parent_game: Cram, a pencil-and-paper game

credits.by: Traditional; popularised by Martin Gardner in Scientific American

equipment: a pen each, in two colours if you have them
intro: Players take turns shading a domino, two squares side by side, on a small grid. If you cannot place a domino on your turn, you lose.

steps.title: Grid
steps.body: Draw a grid of 4 by 4 squares. The usual size is 4 by 6; 4 by 4 makes a quicker game.

steps.title: Place a domino
steps.body: Toss a coin to see who starts. On your turn, shade two empty squares next to each other, across or down.

steps.title: No overlaps
steps.body: A domino may not cover a square already shaded or go off the grid.

steps.title: Last move
steps.body: If you cannot place a domino on your turn, you lose.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Again
steps.body: Play a few times and notice when the grid splits into separate parts.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: When could you count the moves left?
Did a move in the middle split the grid?
Did going second help?

animation.narration: A 4 by 4 grid. P1 shades first.
P1 shades the top-left pair. P2 shades the matching pair in the opposite corner.
P1 goes down the left side; P2 does the same on the right.
P2 keeps copying P1's move, turned half way round the centre.
P1 takes the last pair at the top, P2 the last pair at the bottom. P1 has no move left and loses.

questions.question: What does a domino cover?
options: Two squares next to each other, across or down
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 2.

questions.question: Who loses?
options: The player who cannot place a domino
The player who places the last domino
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 4.

questions.question: What did P2 do on every move?
options: Copied P1's move on the opposite side of the centre
questions.feedback_correct: Right. On a grid with even sides, copying always leaves P2 a move.
questions.feedback_wrong: Compare each of P2's dominoes with P1's.

questions.question: On a 4 by 4 grid P2 can always win by copying. If you wanted to take that away, what would you change?
options: Shade one corner square before starting
Let the loser go second next time
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. An odd side or a missing square breaks the copying; longer pieces change the counting; swapping who goes second only shares the advantage. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: SOS — write S or O, make SOS
parent_game: SOS, a pencil-and-paper game
intro: Players take turns writing an S or an O in an empty square. Make S-O-S in a line and you score and go again. Every letter you write may also set up your opponent.

steps.title: Grid
steps.body: Draw a grid of 4 by 4 squares.

steps.title: Write a letter
steps.body: Toss a coin to see who starts. On your turn, write S or O in any empty square. You may choose a different letter each turn.

steps.title: Score
steps.body: If your letter completes S-O-S in a straight line, across, down or diagonally, you score a point for each new SOS and take another turn.

steps.title: Full grid
steps.body: When every square is filled, the higher score wins. Equal scores are a draw.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><rect x='45' y='12' width='110' height='96' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='58' y='34' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P1  3</text><text x='58' y='54' font-family='IBM Plex Mono' font-size='10' fill='#2D3127'>P2  2</text></svg>

steps.title: Careful
steps.body: An S, an O and an empty square in a line, or two S's with an empty square between them, is a gift to your opponent.

what_to_notice: When did you write a letter only to avoid giving a gift?
Did the extra turn after scoring change the game?
How did the end feel when every square left was dangerous?

animation.narration: P1 writes S in the top-left corner.
P2 writes O next to it.
P1 writes S after it: S-O-S across the top. P1 scores and goes again.
P1 writes O in the bottom-left corner. An O in a corner can never be the middle of an SOS, so it gives nothing away.
Play goes on until all 16 squares are filled. The higher score wins.

questions.question: Which letters may you write?
options: S or O, your choice each turn
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 2.

questions.question: What happens when you complete an SOS?
options: You score a point and take another turn
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: Why was P2's O beside P1's S a mistake?
options: It left S-O with an empty square after it, so P1 could finish SOS
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at what P1 did next.

questions.question: If you wanted fewer gifts and more planning, what would you change?
options: Give each player a fixed letter
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Dropping the extra turn makes a gift cost less; a fixed letter turns it into a different game; a bigger grid gives more safe squares for longer. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Three Men's Morris — three in a row, then move
parent_game: Three Men's Morris, an old game related to tic-tac-toe

credits.rules: The board as recorded by the US National Park Service

equipment: paper and a pen to draw the board
3 coins or pebbles each, of two kinds
intro: Like tic-tac-toe, but with only three pieces each. Once all six are down you slide pieces along the lines, so the game does not stop with a full board.

steps.title: Board
steps.body: Draw a square with nine points: the four corners, the middle of each side and the centre. Join them with lines across, down, and through the centre along both diagonals.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'><rect x='60' y='15' width='80' height='90' fill='none'/><line x1='100' y1='15' x2='100' y2='105'/><line x1='60' y1='60' x2='140' y2='60'/><line x1='60' y1='15' x2='140' y2='105'/><line x1='140' y1='15' x2='60' y2='105'/></g><circle cx='60' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='60' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='60' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/></svg>

steps.title: Place
steps.body: Toss a coin to see who starts. Take turns placing one piece on an empty point. Three of yours in a straight line wins at once.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'><rect x='60' y='15' width='80' height='90' fill='none'/><line x1='100' y1='15' x2='100' y2='105'/><line x1='60' y1='60' x2='140' y2='60'/><line x1='60' y1='15' x2='140' y2='105'/><line x1='140' y1='15' x2='60' y2='105'/></g><circle cx='60' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='60' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='60' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/></svg>

steps.title: Move
steps.body: When all six pieces are down, take turns sliding one of your pieces along a line to an empty point next to it. No jumping.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'><rect x='60' y='15' width='80' height='90' fill='none'/><line x1='100' y1='15' x2='100' y2='105'/><line x1='60' y1='60' x2='140' y2='60'/><line x1='60' y1='15' x2='140' y2='105'/><line x1='140' y1='15' x2='60' y2='105'/></g><circle cx='60' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='15' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='60' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='60' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='60' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='100' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><circle cx='140' cy='105' r='5' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/></svg>

steps.title: Win
steps.body: The first to make a straight line of three wins.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

steps.title: Draw
steps.body: If the same position keeps coming back, or after 20 moves each, call it a draw.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(55,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(145,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: Did the first piece in the centre matter?
When did you make two threats at once?
How did the game change once pieces started moving?

animation.narration: P1 places in the centre.
P2 places top middle.
P1 places top-left, threatening the diagonal.
P2 blocks at bottom-right.
P1 places bottom-left: two threats at once, the left side and the other diagonal.
P2 can block only one, and places top-right.
All six are down. P1 slides the centre piece left, making three down the left side. P1 wins.

questions.question: What happens after all six pieces are placed?
options: Players slide one piece along a line to an empty point next to it
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: Why could P2 not stop P1?
options: P1 made two threats at once and P2 could block only one
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look at the frame where P1 places bottom-left.

questions.question: How did P1 finish the line?
options: Slid the centre piece to the left side
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Compare the last two frames.

questions.question: If you wanted the first player to have less of an advantage, what would you change?
options: The first piece may not go in the centre
The second player gets four pieces
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Banning the centre removes the strongest opening; an extra piece helps the second player; jumping makes lines harder to hold. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: Set — three that all match or all differ
parent_game: SET, a card game designed by Marsha J. Falco

credits.by: Marsha J. Falco, 1974; published by Set Enterprises
credits.version: Homemade and without shading: 27 cards instead of 81

equipment: 27 paper cards you draw: one for every mix of number (1, 2 or 3), shape (diamond, oval, squiggle) and colour (red, green, purple)
intro: Twelve cards lie face up. Everyone looks at once for three cards where every feature is either the same on all three or different on all three. Whoever sees one first and calls 'Set!' takes it. There are no turns.

steps.title: Make 27 cards
steps.body: Draw one card for every mix of number (1, 2 or 3), shape (diamond, oval, squiggle) and colour (red, green, purple), with every shape filled in. The published game adds a fourth feature, shading, and has 81 cards.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-9.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>◆</text></g><g transform='rotate(-3.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>●●</text></g><g transform='rotate(3.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>≈≈≈</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Lay out twelve
steps.body: Shuffle and lay twelve cards face up.

steps.title: Find a set
steps.body: A set is three cards where, for each feature, the three are all the same or all different. Everyone looks at once.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='rotate(-9.0 57 100)'><rect x='40' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='57' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>●</text></g><g transform='rotate(-3.0 91 100)'><rect x='74' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='91' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#2D3127'>●●</text></g><g transform='rotate(3.0 125 100)'><rect x='108' y='28' width='34' height='50' rx='3' fill='white' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='125' y='59' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='16' font-weight='600' fill='#C75B39'>●●●</text></g></svg>

steps.title: Call it
steps.body: Say 'Set!' and point to the three cards. If you are right, take them and lay three new cards. If you are wrong, give back one set you hold, or pay another penalty agreed before you start.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(50,65)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><rect x='75' y='14' width='115' height='34' rx='17' fill='#FFF8E8' stroke='#D9883D' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='132' y='36' text-anchor='middle' font-family='Fraunces' font-size='13' font-style='italic' fill='#7A4A1F'>Set!</text></svg>

steps.title: End
steps.body: If nobody can find a set, lay out three more cards. When the cards run out and no set is left, whoever has the most sets wins; equal counts are a draw.
steps.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 200 120' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><g transform='translate(30,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#C75B39'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#C75B39' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(80,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(130,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g><g transform='translate(175,55)'><circle cx='0' cy='-15' r='8' fill='#2D3127'/><line x1='0' y1='-7' x2='0' y2='15' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='-12' y1='0' x2='12' y2='0' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='-8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/><line x1='0' y1='15' x2='8' y2='30' stroke='#2D3127' stroke-width='3' stroke-linecap='round'/></g></svg>

what_to_notice: How did you look: card by card, or at the whole table?
Did you learn to check one feature at a time?
How did it feel when someone else kept calling first?

animation.narration: Twelve cards. R, G and P are the colours: red, green, purple. Everyone looks at once.
P2 calls 'Set!': two green ovals, one purple oval, three red ovals. Shape the same; number and colour all different. P2 takes them.
Three new cards fill the gaps.
P1 calls 'Set!': one red diamond, two green diamonds, three purple diamonds. P1 takes them.
P3 calls 'Set!' on one red squiggle, two red squiggles and one green squiggle. Not a set: two are red and one is green. P3 pays the agreed penalty.

questions.question: When are three cards a set?
options: When they match in every feature
When each feature is either the same on all three or different on all three
When they are the same colour
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: Is 'one red squiggle, two red squiggles, one green squiggle' a set?
options: No, because the colours are two of one and one of another
No, because the shapes are all the same
Yes, because the shapes are all the same
questions.feedback_correct: Right. Colour is neither all the same nor all different, and number fails the same way.
questions.feedback_wrong: Check colour on its own: red, red, green.

questions.question: Do players take turns?
options: No: everyone looks at once, and the first to call takes the set
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at the introduction.

questions.question: If you wanted a slower player to find sets too, what would you change?
options: Take turns, with a time limit
Give a point for spotting someone's wrong call
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. Turns remove the race but slow everything down; fewer cards make sets rarer; pairs share both the looking and the speed. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.

title: 3 Quarters — complete the three-quarter circle
parent_game: 3 Quarters, a board game by Prayas Abhinav

credits.by: Prayas Abhinav, 2022, as a warm-up game for students
credits.rules: Rules, board and pieces at github.com/prayasabhinav/games, under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0

equipment: the board, printed from https://github.com/prayasabhinav/games/raw/main/3-quarters/3-quarters-board.pdf : 3 columns by 8 rows of squares; play on the red rows with 2 players, add the green rows for 3, and the blue row for 4; the yellow squares double a circle's score

the pieces, printed from https://github.com/prayasabhinav/games/raw/main/3-quarters/3-quarters-pieces.pdf and cut out: for each player, 8 quarter circles, two each of crosshatched (1 point), dotted (2), plain (3) and black (4)
a phone to time each move
intro: '3 Quarters' is a warm up game. One is receptive, when one is perceiving risk. In '3 Quarters' we constantly feel risk. The risk of some move we are making being helpful to other players and contributing to their winning the round is something all players are mindful of.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.body: Arrange one (add, rotate or remove) quadrant at a time to complete a 3/4 circle.

steps.title: A turn
steps.body: In a turn each player gets to arrange (add, rotate or remove) one piece. You can turn as many corners as the dice (d4) shows. If the dice show 4, you have to turn full circle.

steps.title: Remove
steps.body: To remove a quadrant, place a quadrant with the same pattern on it. Take both (without adding the points that both pieces have). A player can remove a piece only three times in a game.

steps.title: Score a circle
steps.body: The player who completes the 3/4 circle removes the pieces from the board and takes as many points as the constituent pieces.

steps.title: Yellow squares
steps.body: If a 3/4 circle has one of its quadrants on a yellow square, the score is doubled.

steps.title: Win
steps.body: The player with 25 points first wins.

steps.title: Keep the board
steps.body: Avoid emptying the board — it will give you a penalty of 10 points.

steps.title: Twenty seconds
steps.body: Each move has to be made in 20 s. Use a mobile to keep time.

what_to_notice: When did a move of yours help another player finish a circle?
How did the 20-second limit change your play?
Was 25 points too quick a target, or about right?

title: All or Nothing — play a slice, win a pizza
parent_game: All or Nothing, a card game by Prayas Abhinav

credits.by: Prayas Abhinav; cards, rules and box made in 2020
credits.rules: Rules and print files at github.com/prayasabhinav/games

equipment: 48 cards: print them from https://github.com/prayasabhinav/games/raw/main/all-or-nothing/print/all-or-nothing-cards.pdf (one card to a page) with the back from https://github.com/prayasabhinav/games/raw/main/all-or-nothing/print/all-or-nothing-card-back.pdf , or write them on paper: green +1 (6 cards), +2 (12), +3 (6); red −1, −2 and −3 (2 each); black ±4, ±5, ±6 and ±7 (4 each); one 'On the house' card and one 'Double order' card
intro: Each player tries to complete a 12-slice pizza by adding or removing slices. In this simple arithmetic game, all age-groups can have quick fun. Adding or subtracting pizza slices feels like the tussle for resources that we face in life. This tussle can be won by individuals who wait and watch — with alertness, foresight and luck. Winning too early, gives less points (as the number of cards in the play space decide the points).

steps.title: Party scene
steps.body: There is a 12-slice pizza on the table. All the players want the entire pizza to themselves. Each player holds 4 cards; the other cards are the deck.

steps.title: A turn
steps.body: Play one card into the centre and pick one card from the deck. Start the game with any green card.

steps.title: The cards
steps.body: Green cards add slices. Red cards remove slices. Black cards add or remove, as you wish; say which while playing.

steps.title: Say the count
steps.body: After playing a card, say the number of pizza slices in the centre: '3 + 2 = 5'. The number of slices cannot be less than 0 or more than 12.

steps.title: Extra hungry cards
steps.body: Double order: the players have to complete 24 slices to win this round. On the house: a coupon for this round; if you complete the pizza, you score double the number of cards in the centre, and if another player completes it, your card is wasted.

steps.title: Win a round
steps.body: Whoever completes the 12 slices wins the round and scores one point for each card in the centre. Shuffle all the cards except those in players' hands, and begin the next round. The game can continue till you are full with pizzas.

steps.title: Two ways to play
steps.body: Simple: hold your 4 cards in your hand, hidden. Challenge: place your 4 cards face up for the other players to see. Knowing everyone's cards means you have to plan ahead to win, but it also means more points.

what_to_notice: When did you hold back from completing the pizza, to let the centre grow?
Did a red card feel like taking a slice from someone?
How did the Challenge way, with cards face up, change your play?

animation.narration: Four players hold 4 cards each. The pizza is empty: 0 slices. The first card has to be green.
P1 plays green +3: '0 + 3 = 3', and draws a card.
P2 plays green +2: '3 + 2 = 5'.
P3 plays a black 4 and adds it: '5 + 4 = 9'.
P4 plays red −2: '9 − 2 = 7'. Nobody gets the pizza yet.
P1 plays a black 5 and adds it: '7 + 5 = 12'. P1 completes the pizza. Five cards are in the centre, so P1 scores 5.

questions.question: What does a red card do?
options: Adds or removes, as you say
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: Look again at step 3.

questions.question: The count is 9 and P4 plays red −2. What do they say?
questions.feedback_correct: Right.
questions.feedback_wrong: A red card takes slices away.

questions.question: How many points did P1 score for completing the pizza?
questions.feedback_correct: Right: one point for each of the five cards in the centre.
questions.feedback_wrong: Count the cards played this round.

questions.question: Winning too early gives fewer points. If you wanted players to wait even longer before completing the pizza, what would you change?
options: Score double for a round longer than ten cards
Let the pizza be 24 slices every round
Make every card in the centre worth two points
questions.feedback_correct: There is no single answer. A bonus for long rounds rewards waiting; a bigger pizza slows every round; passing lets a player wait without changing the count. Talk about which you would try, and what it would change.
